pairs.locus: Plautus, Curculio (quoted at Varro, De Lingua Latina 7.2)
pairs.question: Sed quid tibi est?
pairs.answer: Lien enecat, renes dolent, pulmones distrahuntur.
pairs.derivation: A two-speaker exchange from Curculio quoted by Varro to illustrate dividia/distrahuntur. The editorial speaker-change dash (—) was stripped as a drama marker. Question kept as the first speaker's full contiguous utterance (interrogative quid tibi est?). Answer is the second speaker's reply, which genuinely answers by listing the ailments; no preamble to skip and nothing follows the reply in the quoted fragment.

pairs.question: Quid noctis videtur?
pairs.answer: In altisono caeli clipeo temo superat stellas sublimen agens etiam atque etiam noctis iter.
pairs.derivation: Interrogative quid noctis videtur? ('what time of night is it?') answered by a description of the temo (Wain) overtopping the stars, which Varro glosses as indicating deep night (Hic multam noctem ostendere volt a temonis motu). The editorial speaker-change dash was stripped; verse line-initial capitals (In, Caeli, Stellas, Atque) were lowercased as presentation normalization. Answer is the full contiguous reply through the verse fragment; nothing of the utterance was ellipted.
